note: Rendered carriageway width against the city's kerb lines, from scripts/audit_corridor_render.py (widthVsKerb). tests/test_width_vs_kerb.py fails when a build gets worse than this; regenerate deliberately with `python scripts/audit_corridor_render.py --baseline` after a change that improves it.
tooNarrowNote: 184 -> 190 when the building-line clamp landed: six alleys with no kerb lines of their own, whose 'kerb' here is the avenue's across the block. Narrower is right for them.
crosswalkAttachedShareNote: 0.902 -> 0.875 when every kerb became the one an unmeasured kerb gets (KERB_RENDER_UNIFORM, 2026-09-27). A crossing leg is placed against the kerb the survey read station by station; the kerb is now drawn at the way's single width, so 2.7% of legs no longer land exactly on it. That is the price of the uniform kerb and it was paid on purpose -- the measured path is the one that drops corner pieces and leaves a staircase of disconnected slabs at junctions like Pine and Stockton. Every other measure held: width vs kerb 0.030 m, ways enveloped 1652 of 1653, ramps 0.873, cross-sections 0.746.
